articles.title: Miss Brasil Supranational 2026 perde posto ao anunciar gravidez | G1
articles.standfirst: Concurso Nacional de Beleza disse que Lara Marina Soares Tosta perdeu o título após "descumprimento de obrigações contratuais". Vice-campeã assumirá a coroa.
articles.summary: Concurso Nacional de Beleza disse que Lara Marina Soares Tosta perdeu o título após "descumprimento de obrigações contratuais". Vice-campeã assumirá a coroa.
articles.body:
A modelo Lara Marina Soares Tosta, Miss Brasil Supranational 2026 , anunciou nas redes sociais, nesta quarta-feira (26), que perdeu o posto por estar grávida . Lara Marina tem 19 anos, é de Afonso Cláudio , na Região Serrana do Espírito Santo, e conquistou o título nacional na competição realizada em Pernambuco, em fevereiro.

Antes do pronunciamento dela, o organizador da competição, Concurso Nacional de Beleza (CNB), publicou nas redes sociais a perda do título sem explicar os motivos da decisão. Horas depois, a ex-Miss publicou um vídeo e revelou que está grávida.

O CNB informou que aconteceu um "descumprimento de obrigações contratuais consideradas incompatíveis com a manutenção do título".

Já Lara contou que a gestação foi descoberta após seu retorno do concurso Miss Supranational 2026, realizado na Polônia, no qual conquistou o terceiro lugar.

Ao g1 , nesta quinta-feira (27), Lara disse que não tem nada além para falar. "No vídeo está todo meu depoimento de coração para coração" .

Lara Marina, capixaba e ex-Miss Supranational 2026 — Foto: Redes sociais

No vídeo, Lara agradeceu o carinho dos fãs e da família e informou que a gravidez não é o fim da trajetória, mas sim o "começo de um novo capítulo".

"Apesar de todas as circunstâncias e de tudo o que aconteceu nos últimos dias, eu posso dizer com muita alegria que eu sou uma futura mãe [...] isso não cancela a minha história, não apaga tudo que eu construí ou tudo aquilo que eu representei", disse a ex-Miss Brasil Supranational.

A modelo também destacou ter orgulho e respeito pelo título e disse ter uma nova razão para continuar aprendendo a ser uma "melhor versão" de si mesma.

"Escolho continuar de uma forma diferente, em um novo caminho, mas ainda sendo eu", concluiu.

Eduarda Braum, Miss Supranational 2025 e primeira brasileira a conquistar o título , fez uma publicação em apoio à ex-Miss. Ela parabenizou a trajetória da conterrânea e afirmou: "sempre poderá contar comigo".

"No palco internacional, eu olhei para você, extremamente emocionada, e disse o quanto estava orgulhosa [...] por ver você representando a nossa cidade, nosso estado e o Brasil com tanto amor e dedicação. A família Supranational sempre estará com você, você sempre fará parte dela", disse.

Outras misses também compartilharam mensagens de apoio a Lara nas redes sociais. "Sempre com você", disse a Miss Supranational Equador 2026 e Miss Intercontinental América do Sul 2025, Kika Marques Das Neves.

"Uma bênção chegou e meu coração não poderia estar mais feliz. Amo você. Parabéns, minha linda irmã, a maternidade fica linda em você", compartilhou a Miss Supranational Camboja 2026, Hok Sarytola.

O comunicado do CNB explicou que a nova representante do concurso é a Miss Costa Verde e Mar, Camilly Ceccon, que ficou em segundo lugar na competição. A coroação oficial da nova miss ainda não teve data divulgada.

A última participação de Lara nos concursos aconteceu na final do Miss Supranational 2026, realizada na Polônia em julho. A capixaba terminou a competição em terceiro lugar e quem levou a coroa principal foi a representante das Filipinas, Katrina Llegado.

Comunicado do Concurso Nacional de Beleza informou que a Miss Brasil Supranational 2026, Lara Marina Soares Tosta, perdeu o título — Foto: Redes sociais

Em fevereiro, a modelo capixaba Lara Marina, de 19 anos e 1,85 m de altura, foi eleita a Miss Supranational Brasil 2026 quando venceu a etapa nacional da competição em Pernambuco.

Nos concursos de beleza, a trajetória da capixaba, que também é estudante universitária de Publicidade e Propaganda, começou há menos de um ano, quando ela foi eleita Miss Afonso Cláudio e, em seguida, Miss ES Supranational.

No ano passado, Lara também ficou em segundo lugar na disputa pelo Miss Universe Espírito Santo.

A modelo do Espírito Santo Lara Marina, de 19 anos, foi eleita a Miss Supranational Brasil 2026 — Foto: Divulgação

Aclamada para representar o estado na franquia Supranational, a modelo competiu com outras 19 mulheres de diferentes regiões do país e revelou, na pergunta final, que transformou sua vida após ressignificar o bullying que sofreu na escola, por causa da altura, nas competições de miss.

"Quando pequena, sofri bullying na escola em relação à minha altura, e foi através dos concursos de beleza que consegui ressignificar toda a minha jornada. Encontrei a minha melhor força, minha melhor versão, e hoje estar aqui neste palco é a materialização de um sonho que vai continuar."

Lara Marina é natural de Afonso Cláudio, no Espírito Santo. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

articles.title: Creche suspende atividades após surto de sarna em MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao todo, foram identificados 25 casos. Todos os alunos e funcionários da Cemei Professora Maria Conceição Carvalho, em Alfenas, bem como seus familiares, foram medicados.
articles.summary: Ao todo, foram identificados 25 casos. Todos os alunos e funcionários da Cemei Professora Maria Conceição Carvalho, em Alfenas, bem como seus familiares, foram medicados.
articles.body:
As atividades da Cemei Professora Maria Conceição Carvalho, conhecida como Dona Zínica, em Alfenas (MG) foram interrompidas temporariamente por medida de segurança após ser comprovado um surto de escabiose, conhecida como sarna humana, que atingiu alunos e servidores.

Cemei Professora Maria Conceição Carvalho, em Alfenas — Foto: Reprodução EPTV

De acordo com a Secretária Municipal de Educação, Thays Alexandre Salles, a creche já havia sido fechada na segunda-feira (24), após a identificação de três casos, e passou por limpeza. Mas, após o retorno na quarta-feira (26), uma inspeção da Secretaria de Saúde encontrou mais funcionários e alunos com sintomas de escabiose.

Diante do risco de transmissão, a prefeitura decidiu suspender novamente as aulas, a princípio, por sete dias para higienização e controle do surto.

Ao todo, foram confirmados 25 casos de sarna humana no local, sendo 19 estudantes e seis servidores.

Todos os 58 servidores e 180 alunos, com exceção de bebês com menos de 15 kg, estão sendo medicados e acompanhados pelas equipes de saúde.

"Quando nós retornamos, em comum acordo com a Vigilância Epidemiológica, solicitamos para que a equipe médica fosse até o local para verificar a situação da escola, dos nossos alunos, para dar segurança para as crianças, para as famílias e para os nossos servidores, e mais alguns casos foram diagnosticados. Com isso, nós suspendemos hoje as aulas e vamos suspender por mais sete dias para dar tempo de fazer a segunda dose do medicamento", disse a secretária.

A coordenadora de Vigilância em Saúde e Epidemiologia de Alfenas, Thaila Zatiti, explicou que o tratamento também vai ser feito com os familiares das pessoas que foram afetadas.

"A transmissão é muito rápida, basta um contato em um ambiente mais fechado, de 15 a 20 minutos, para que a gente possa transmitir e o outro possa ser contaminado. Em todos os casos que foram diagnosticados, nós tratamos também os familiares. Não adianta tratar só os sintomáticos, precisa tratar todos aqueles que têm contato próximo com os casos diagnosticados para cortar essa cadeia de transmissão", disse Thaila.

Escabiose, doença popularmente conhecida como sarna, afeitou crianças e servidores em creche de Alfenas — Foto: Freepik

Escabiose ou sarna humana é uma doença parasitária que provoca lesões na pele e coceira intensa. É causada por um ácaro e é altamente contagiosa. Sua transmissão é feita pelo contato direto com a pessoa infectada, roupas ou objetos contaminados.

A Sociedade Brasileira de Dermatologia reforça que a doença não tem relação com falta de higiene e não é transmitida por cães ou gatos.

A coceira ocorre principalmente à noite e atinge os dedos e palma das mãos, punhos, mamilos, coxas e genitais, mas podendo ser generalizada.

O tratamento é feito normalmente por meio de medicações tópica. Todas as pessoas que tiveram contato direto com a pessoa diagnosticada devem ser examinadas e tratadas se estiverem infectadas, para interromper a cadeia de transmissão.

articles.title: ‘Need is not to eliminate tanks, but to modernise them’: Rajnath Singh on India’s armoured warfare push
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday said tanks continue to remain relevant in modern warfare despite the growing use of drones, miss.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday said tanks continue to remain relevant in modern warfare despite the growing use of drones, missiles, satellites, artificial intelligence and cyber warfare, stressing the need to modernise armoured platforms rather than phase them out.Speaking in Jabalpur, Singh said the role of tanks had evolved with changes in technology and the character of warfare, but their requirement in ground combat had not disappeared."The role of tanks has not ended; the role of tanks is evolving. Technology is changing and the character of warfare is changing, but the need for tanks in ground combat has not ended. And this is also guiding our defence policy," Singh said.He said the strength of tanks lies in the combination of mobility, protection and firepower, allowing them to provide protected mobility to soldiers even in difficult terrain."Everyone has their own strength. For example, the biggest strength of a tank is the combination of its mobility, protection and firepower. It provides protected mobility to soldiers even in difficult terrain. At the same time, tanks can play a decisive role in ground operations," he said.Singh said the focus should be on equipping tanks with advanced technologies and capabilities suited to modern battlefields."Therefore, the need today is not to eliminate tanks, but to modernise them. They need to be equipped with better sensors and capabilities suited to modern battlefield requirements," he said."Today, the character of warfare has certainly changed. There are drones, precision-guided weapons, missiles, satellites, artificial intelligence and cyber warfare. But this does not mean that the relevance of tanks has ended. Modern warfare is not about any single platform," he said.The Defence Minister said tanks would form part of an integrated combat system alongside infantry, artillery, drones, air power, surveillance and precision weapons."Tank, infantry, artillery, drones, air power, surveillance and precision weapons, all of these together form an integrated combat system. An example of this approach has been presented by our Army in the form of the Integrated Battle Group," he said.Singh was speaking at the foundation stone ceremony for a strategic facility at Vehicle Factory Jabalpur for the overhaul of T-72 and T-90 tanks."At Vehicle Factory, Jabalpur, I congratulate all of you on the foundation stone laying ceremony for the strategic facility for the overhaul of T-72 and T-90 tanks. Today is a day to take our industrial self-reliance to a new height and to further enhance the pride of a historic city like Jabalpur on India's defence manufacturing map," he said.He described the project as an important example of India's growing technological capability, industrial capacity and confidence in the defence sector."The facility for which we are laying the foundation stone today is not an ordinary project. It is in itself an example of India's growing technological consciousness, our industrial capability and our increasing confidence in the defence sector," Singh said.He added that the project would benefit soldiers as well as local communities, including farmers, workers, young people and small entrepreneurs."This project will prove to be a boon for our soldiers who use these tanks to destroy the enemy. And most importantly, this project will also bring prosperity and opportunities into the lives of local people in Jabalpur and surrounding areas, our farmers, our workers, our youth and our small entrepreneurs," he said.Singh also highlighted Madhya Pradesh's plans to expand defence manufacturing, saying 3,073 hectares of land in the Gwalior-Chambal region had been identified for defence manufacturing opportunities, with proposed investments exceeding Rs 16,960 crore.

articles.title: Barrier lake near Nepal border could breach in 3 days, China warns as hundreds dead in flash floods
articles.summary: China News: A barrier lake formed near the confluence of the Chhochen Khola and Purepu Tsangpo rivers in Nepal could face a high risk of breaching over the next t.
articles.body: A barrier lake formed near the confluence of the Chhochen Khola and Purepu Tsangpo rivers in Nepal could face a high risk of breaching over the next three days, Global Times reported citing Chinese authorities on Thursday. This comes as hundreds died and thousands remain missing after catastrophic flash floods in the China-Nepal border region.China’s ministry of water resources said the lake had accumulated around 2 million cubic metres of water by Thursday morning and was already overflowing.Another 3 million cubic metres of water is expected to enter the lake over the next three days, raising the risk of a breach, state broadcaster CCTV reported.The ministry said it was closely monitoring the lake and carrying out flood simulations and risk assessments to prepare for a possible breach and support emergency rescue operations.A glacier collapse in Tibet triggered devastating flash floods and mudslides along the China-Nepal border. Authorities in the two countries have reported at least 273 deaths and more than 1,300 people missing, though figures vary between agencies because of differences in data collection, verification and coordination.In Nepal, police reported at least 270 deaths and 826 people missing. The National Tourism Board later said 517 foreigners were among those missing, including tourists and pilgrims in the region.India accounts for the largest number of missing foreign nationals, with 288 people reported missing, most of whom were believed to have been travelling towards Mount Kailash, a sacred Hindu pilgrimage site. The United States reported 65 missing, while Malaysia had 51, Ukraine 53, Australia 35 and Britain 33.In China, state media reported three deaths and 558 people missing in Gyirong County in Tibet, including 260 foreign nationals. China’s foreign ministry also said nearly 100 Chinese citizens were missing on the Nepalese side.Chinese authorities have deployed emergency responders, People's Liberation Army personnel, engineering teams, telecom operators and relief organisations to the affected areas. articles.body: The Nepal flood disaster has claimed at least 270 lives, while more than 800 people have been reported missing. Several survivors have come forward and shared their first-hand accounts of the situation with the media."We saw several bodies, animals in the river. The administration has recovered 10-12 bodies downstream today", a local told news agency PTI.Kalpana Malla from the Nuwakot district, who was saved by her son, recalled her family getting swept away in front of her eyes"They could not escape the flood; there was no chance at all," she told BBC.Sonam Dorjee, who had left for Kathmandu an hour before the flood, described hearing the flood water tearing through his village."It sounded like an earthquake," he said.He further reported his sister and other family members missing, describing the situation as sudden and devastating.Another survivor, Kedar Nath Parajuli, described how the flood water struck him even as he was on the upper floor of a building"We were staying on the upper floor. The flood water rose all the way up, covering the floor with mud", Kedar told the South China Morning Post.The victims of the disaster are not just humans, but animals too.Goma Pandit, said she had lost her buffaloes and all her other cattle."My farmland is also swept away. Ten sacks of mustard seeds, tons of corn and rice paddy are all gone. Nothing is left", she said.How the disaster unfoldedAt about 02.55 GMT on Wednesday, a huge wall of mud and rock collapsed into the Lhende Khola river valley along the Sino-Nepal border, eventually triggering a massive flood.As the water rushed downhill, it engulfed villages, destroyed homes and critical infrastructure, washing away multiple bridges and several kilometres of road.The disaster struck the key pilgrimage route to Kailash Mansarovar, leaving several pilgrims killed, or missing.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Nepal floods: No contact with 290 Indians in Nepal, another 200 stranded on China side - key points
articles.summary: South Asia News: Nepal is battling the aftermath of catastrophic floods and landslides triggered by a glacier collapse, with hundreds killed and more than 1,300 people.
articles.body: Nepal is battling the aftermath of catastrophic floods and landslides triggered by a glacier collapse, with hundreds killed and more than 1,300 people reported missing across Nepal and Tibet. Rescue teams are racing against difficult terrain, damaged roads and bridges, and the risk of further disasters as relief operations continue in the Himalayan region.India has intensified efforts to trace its nationals affected by the disaster, with external affairs minister S Jaishankar reviewing the situation with senior MEA officials and Indian ambassadors in Kathmandu and Beijing. The MEA is coordinating with Nepalese authorities, state governments, tour operators and project agencies to establish the status and well-being of Indians in the affected areas.290 Indians remain unaccountable: MEATwo hundred and ninty Indian nationals remain unaccounted for following the devastating flash floods in Nepal, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the missing Indians included people working on hydropower projects as well as members of tourist groups.Jaiswal also said 21 Indians from Tamil Nadu had been rescued following the floods, while around 200 Indians in Tibet had sought assistance from India.“India is standing shoulder-to-shoulder with Nepal in this difficult time and we are ready to provide all assistance as per requirements of that country,” he added.Jaishankar reviews flood situationJaishankar held a review meeting with foreign secretary Vikram Misri, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal and other officials, as well as India's ambassadors in Kathmandu and Beijing."Held a review meeting with foreign secretary, Team MEA and our ambassadors in Kathmandu & Beijing on the Nepal flood disaster. Urgent efforts are underway to ascertain the status and well-being of all Indians in the flood-affected areas," Jaishankar said in a post on X/"MEA is coordinating with various ministries, state governments, tour operators and project authorities in this regard. We are working closely with the Nepali side, both on this aspect and on the relief efforts," he added.India sends second relief consignmentIndia has dispatched a second tranche of humanitarian assistance to Nepal. Jaishankar said a flight carrying 37.5 tonnes of humanitarian assistance and disaster relief material, medicines and food packets had departed for Nepal.This followed an initial 10-tonne consignment of relief material, including essential medicines, sent on Wednesday. Indian ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava handed over the supplies to Nepal's minister for culture, tourism and civil aviation Khadak Raj Paudel in Kathmandu.Prime Minister Narendra Modi had also spoken with Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Wednesday and offered India's support for rescue and relief operations.Hundreds killed, more than 1,300 missingThe disaster has killed at least 359 people in Nepal and left 826 missing, while three people have died and 558 remain missing in Tibet, according to authorities cited in reports.Nepal's army has rescued more than 100 people through helicopter operations, while at least eight foreign nationals were airlifted to Kathmandu. Dozens of bridges and nearly 40 km of roads were damaged, complicating rescue operations.Helpline numbers have been initiated to help those in need.Glacier collapse behind deadly floodsThe US geological survey later determined that the event initially reported as an earthquake was a magnitude 5.2 glacier collapse that sent a destructive torrent downstream.Experts at the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development said an avalanche from a glacier likely triggered the flash flood. Water levels in the Trishuli river rose by as much as 9 metres within half an hour, underscoring the speed and scale of the disaster.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Number of asylum seekers in hotels halves in a year, data shows
articles.summary: Figures released today by the Home Office show that there was also a fall across legal migration arrivals, asylum claims and small boat arrivals.
articles.body:
There has been a significant fall in the use of hotels to house asylum seekers waiting for a Home Office decision, data shows.

In June 2025 there were more than 32,000 people in hotel rooms, but by June this year it had halved to more than 16,000.

There has also been a drop in legal migration arrivals, asylum claims and small boat arrivals to the UK compared to a year ago.

The Home Office said the figures showed that policies to control migration were having an effect - but said there was still more to do on the issue of small boat crossings.

Track UK's latest migration numbers - net migration, visas, asylum and small boats

There was also a fall in the number of family members coming to the UK to join someone already legally in the country, while asylum claims were also down by a fifth.

Some 38,000 illegal arrivals were detected in the year to June - 33,000 of them on small boats across the sea from France.

More up to date figures show the trend in small boat arrivals has continued to be lower than last year. Correspondingly, claims for asylum have also fallen.

Some 86,000 people sought asylum - down a fifth on the previous year. About half of those applications for help came from people who were already legally in the UK, rather than having arrived on a small boat.

The rise in the use of hotels coincided with an increase in arrivals across the English Channel from 2019 and a slowing down of Home Office decisions as to how many of these claimants had a genuine right to stay in the UK or should be told to leave.

One of the first decisions of the new Starmer government in July 2024 was to order officials to work faster in deciding these claims, with a target of ending the use of hotels within five years.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said: "A little over two years into office and the asylum backlog is down, the number of asylum seekers in hotels is falling, illegal working arrests are at record levels, and deportations and returns are up markedly.

"Small boats numbers are also now falling, but we are not complacent and there is more we must do."

Shadow home secretary Chris Philp said Labour was "moving illegal immigrants out of hotels and into flats in your building."

He said a Conservative government would deport every illegal immigrant and leave the European Court of Human Rights.

"The surest way to empty the accommodation is to make plain that nobody who crosses the Channel gets to stay," he added.

In response to the new figures, Reform UK said Britain was at "breaking point".

Zia Yusuf, its home affairs spokesman, said "Under Reform, illegal boats in the Channel will be stopped by our Navy, and all those here illegally will be detained and deported."

The number of people in houses around the country paid for by the Home Office has gone up from 65,000 at the end of 2024 to 69,000 in June this year - arrangements that are part of a decade-long standing contract with private providers.

The number of asylum claimants waiting for an initial ruling on their case - meaning they are told whether they have a genuine case for protection or should leave the UK - was 40,000. That is down from the peak of 175,000 in June 2023.

Meanwhile some 40,000 found not to have a reason to be in the UK - either foreign offenders, visa overstayers or failed asylum applicants - were removed from the country in the year to June 2026, an 8% increase on the year before.

Officials say about a third were failed asylum seekers - the highest number for 16 years and double the rate of removals that occurred in 2021.

The statistics also show 235,000 work visas in the year to the end of June 2026 by the Home Office. That is down 18% on the previous year and 62% lower than the peak in December 2023.

That high related to policies followed by the former prime minister Boris Johnson to liberalise the work visa system - but in its dying months the Rishi Sunak government tightened the rules.

Significantly, the number of workers who could arrive on a specialist health and care worker visa fell by 90% - following progressive tightening of that route.

The data also reveals 383,000 foreign students came to the UK in the year to June 2026 - down 11% on the previous year and 41% down on the peak in June 2023.

Following the introduction of restrictions on how migrants could apply to bring family members to join them, only 58,000 such visas were granted in the year to June 2026 - 19% down on the previous 12 months.

Statisticians say that the fall was "largely driven" by new rules making it exceptionally hard for refugee families to come together in the UK. That policy - which has faced challenges in the High Court - remains in place with the government believing it has an impact on deterring illegal arrivals across the English Channel.

Critics say it denies genuine refugees the chance to rebuild their lives.

Immigration stats are published every three months, and related to a 12-month period.

articles.title: In the 1950s, a Chinese American Army veteran turned a New York mountain into a ski resort; in 2026, its 440 acres were bought for $3.3 million to join a state park
articles.summary: US News: In the 1950s, Chinese American Army veteran Joseph Tso bought a 440-acre mountain property in Ellenville, New York, renamed it Mt Cathalia and develop.
articles.body: In the 1950s, Chinese American Army veteran Joseph Tso bought a 440-acre mountain property in Ellenville, New York, renamed it Mt Cathalia and developed a hotel and ski resort there. The property is now set to become part of Minnewaska State Park Preserve. According to Open Space Institute, the property was bought for $3.3 million and will connect two previously separated sections of the park.Mt Cathalia, also known as Mt Meenagha is the largest remaining undeveloped, privately owned parcel adjoining Minnewaska. According to Chonogram Magazine, OSI bought it from Morgan Barrington Financial Services and plans to transfer the land to New York State for inclusion in the park’s Sam’s Point Area.The property lies between Minnewaska’s North and South Gully areas, near the Ellenville Ice Caves and its addition will connect sections of protected land that were previously unlinked. The preserve would also grow to more than 24,000 acres once the transfer is completed.The place's Chinese American historyThe mountain’s history is one reason the acquisition has drawn attention beyond its conservation value. In the 1950s, Joseph Tso, a Chinese American attorney, businessman and US Army veteran, purchased the property and renamed it Mt. Cathalia, meaning 'a little bit of China'.Tso then established a hotel and ski area on the mountain. According to OSI, Mt. Cathalia became the country’s only Chinese American-owned and operated ski resort and hotel.The resort welcomed Chinese Americans and other minority visitors who were excluded from many resorts during that period.According to Tso’s children, Cecilia and Stan Tso, the property continues to have deep meaning for their family. “Mt. Cathalia means so much to our family. We are hoping that OSI’s efforts will fulfil our parents’ dream of sharing Mt. Cathalia with everyone,” they said.Connecting protected areasThe 440-acre property sits between the North and South Gully areas of Minnewaska. Its acquisition will create a link between the two sections near the Ellenville Ice Caves.Erik Kulleseid, president and CEO of OSI, says, “Mt Cathalia is an extraordinary landscape on every level- environmentally, recreationally, and historically”. He describes the purchase as another step towards creating “a corridor of permanently conserved and connected land along the entire Shawangunk Ridge.”OSI has been involved in conservation work in the Shawangunks since 1974. The organisation says it has protected more than 40,000 acres in the region and helped add 14,000 acres to Minnewaska, more than doubling the park’s size.Its work has also included restoring nearly 18 miles of Minnewaska’s historic carriage roads and raising $3 million for the Lake Minnewaska Visitor Center, which opened in 2020.Ski runs become meadowsThe property's former ski runs have now become meadows surrounded by mature chestnut oak and pine forests. Mt Cathalia contains Shawangunk conglomerate outcrops and gullies lined with hemlock trees. OSI estimates that nearly the entire property has above-average habitat resilience. It says the mountain’s different elevations and microclimates could provide wildlife refuge as the climate changes.The land is also part of the Sandburg Creek watershed. North Gully serves as an emergency drinking-water source for Ellenville, while water from both North and South Gully eventually flows towards the Hudson River.According to OSI’s analysis, the property’s forests and soils store an estimated 132,000 metric tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent.Ellenville Mayor Evan Trent says the acquisition protects an important part of the village’s viewshed as well as one of the largest tracts in its watershed. He also hopes the mountain will eventually become a public recreational space.For now, Mt. Cathalia remains closed to visitors. The immediate plan is to complete the transfer and prepare the property for its future as part of Minnewaska State Park Preserve.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Cameroon femicides: Footballer Nchout Njoya Ajara speaks out after eight women killed in a week
articles.summary: The killing of at least eight women in a week has sparked outrage in Cameroon.
articles.body:
The killing of at least eight women in a week has sparked outrage in Cameroon, with many calling on the government to do more to protect women and girls.

Among those who have spoken out is renowned footballer Nchout Njoya Ajara, who has called for an end to the "tragic wave" of targeting women, saying "silence is complicity".

The government has also raised concern about the rise in attacks. At least 50 women have been killed between January and April this year, compared to 77 last year, according to official figures.

In the latest case on Tuesday, a 44-year-old woman was killed in a hotel room in the capital, Yaoundé. She was allegedly stabbed to death by a 22-year-old who was later arrested.

"Being a woman in Cameroon should never be a risk," said Ajara, who is one of Cameroon's greatest female footballers.

The 33-year-old striker has played professionally in Russia, Sweden, Norway, Spain, Italy and Saudi Arabia for clubs including Atlético Madrid and Inter Milan.

"In the face of the tragic wave of femicides that has hit our country in recent days, silence is complicity," Ajara said.

'We are the friend' - inspiring those fleeing terror

In a statement, the opposition Cameroon Renaissance Movement (CRM) party said it was outraged by the "tragic recurrence of domestic femicides" and accused the government of being passive about the issue.

The femicide cases, most of which are attributed to domestic violence, have been reported in different parts of the country.

In a video published by state media, the minister for Women's Empowerment and the Family, Marie-Thérèse Abena Ondoa, condemned the "worrying" rise in the number of the killings, and said the government was working to address the problem.

She mentioned a bill to protect women against gender-based violence, which she said was being reviewed by the prime minister.

But civil society and women's rights groups have denounced what they perceive as the government's delay in turning the bill into law.

A parliamentary session, the last one for the year, is due to be held in November. However, Viviane Tathi, whose organisation documents cases of femicide in the country, told the BBC she was not sure that the bill would be passed at the session.

"We are worried because the November parliamentary session focuses on budgetary debates…So, we don't know by what magic this bill will be passed," she said.

She has called for the creation of a special court to handle family disputes, which lead to domestic violence.

According to the latest UN data, Africa had both the highest total number of femicide victims and the highest rate relative to its population in 2024 - with an estimated 22,600 cases .

The numbers are an estimate as some cases of femicide are believed to go unreported and many governments do not consistently record the information.

articles.title: Red Arrows return for Lyme Regis flypast after display cancelled
articles.summary: The Red Arrows will perform a flypast over Lyme Regis after pulling out of a display.
articles.body:
The Red Arrows will perform a flypast over the Dorset coast, nearly two weeks after a display was cancelled due to them being stranded in Canada.

The RAF aerobatic team had been due to display at the Lyme Regis RNLI Lifeboat Week on 16 August but pulled out after poor weather left them grounded at Goose Bay.

The gap in the schedule was filled by wheelbarrow performance group the Bradninch Red Barrows.

The Red Arrows will fly in formation over the seafront and Lyme Bay at 18:35 BST on Friday but will not perform an aerobatic display.

The Reds originally scheduled the flypast for Saturday lunchtime but the weather forecast and operational constraints have led to an amended timetable.

They said in a Facebook post: "With poor weather into the bank holiday weekend, the Royal Air Force Aerobatic Team will be doing all it can to get to planned events and displays.

"However, due to forecasted conditions, and operational constraints impacting which airfields the Red Arrows will be able to use in the coming days, there will be changes to these scheduled performances."

It said the RAF Wyton Families' Day display in Cambridgeshire on Thursday afternoon had been cancelled, the flypast for Lyme Regis would be at 18:35 on Friday, and the planned Sidmouth Regatta and Airshow display in Devon would now be a flypast at 18:40 on Friday.

Lyme Regis mayor Philip Evans said: "We were naturally disappointed when circumstances outside anyone's control meant the Red Arrows couldn't join us earlier this month, so we're delighted that Lyme Regis has another opportunity to welcome them back to our skies.

"It may only be a brief visit this time, but we're sure it will still be a spectacular sight over Lyme Bay and something residents and visitors will enjoy."

Visitors are urged to use public transport where possible and allow plenty of time for their journey.

The Red Arrows were delayed returning from their tour of the US, resulting in them pulling out of displays, including Lyme Regis Lifeboat Week and Airbourne airshow in Eastbourne, East Sussex.

The jets, which are unable to refuel mid-flight, arrived back in the UK at RAF Lossiemouth in Scotland on 16 August after refuelling stops in Greenland and Iceland.

The Red Barrows, from Bradninch, Devon, describe themselves as an "elite display squadron", performing "precision formation flying through rings of fire, smoke trails and death-defying low passes at air shows across the south west".

articles.title: US citizenship applicants face renewed neighbourhood scrutiny under new USCIS guidance
articles.summary: US News: Those applying for US citizenship could face scrutiny from their neighbours, co-workers and wider communities as the US Citizenship and Immigration Se.
articles.body: Those applying for US citizenship could face scrutiny from their neighbours, co-workers and wider communities as the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has formally laid out how it will conduct neighbourhood investigations during the naturalisation (citizenship) process.The new guidance, issued on Aug 25, took effect immediately and applies to citizenship applications pending on that date as well as those filed thereafter. Investigators may seek information from people who know the applicant, including neighbours, landlords, employers, co-workers, business associates, customers and others. The scope can be wide, covering an applicant's family and marital history, social activities and associations, employment and business activities, financial obligations and reputation in the community.The inquiry may also examine criminal history, international travel and foreign activities, as well as current and previous residences. USCIS may assess an applicant's credibility and truthfulness, loyalty to the US and respect for the principles in the US Constitution.As was reported earlier by TOI, USCIS had resumed such investigations in Aug 2025, after the practice had largely been abandoned in 1991. The latest guidance explains how the investigations may be used to corroborate information supplied by applicants and gather information that may not emerge from documents or the naturalisation interview.Also read: USCIS is empowered to conduct neighbourhood investigations for those applying for US citizenshipHowever, it should be noted that the investigations will not automatically apply to every applicant. USCIS said its ‘Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate’, in coordination with field operations, will decide whether an investigation should be conducted or waived based on an individualised and discretionary assessment of the case.USCIS added that information from members of the community can assist in determining whether an applicant meets citizenship requirements, including good moral character and being well disposed to the good order and happiness of the US.Applicants can voluntarily submit character-reference or testimonial letters with their Form N-400 application. USCIS says such letters, preferably from US citizens who are not family members, may be considered when deciding whether to waive a neighbourhood investigation. However, immigration attorneys point out that even if these letters are submitted, USCIS officials may still decide to speak to neighbours, co-workers, employers and others.For the Indian diaspora, which has navigated lengthy green card waits before becoming eligible for naturalisation, the prospect of a review extending beyond their application papers and citizenship interview could add a layer of uncertainty. Immigration attorneys believe that, by and large, a history of stable employment, regular tax payments and participation in their children's school activities or the wider community could stand Indian applicants in good stead. However, the bottom line is that it remains to be seen how this new guidance will be enforced.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Zambia election: Opposition leader Brian Mundubile questioned by police - state media
articles.summary: Brian Mundubile had been in hiding after disputing the outcome of the recent presidential election.
articles.body:
Zambian opposition leader Brian Mundubile, who had gone into hiding after disputing the recent presidential election result, has been handed over to the police, state broadcaster ZNBC is reporting.

The official results from the 13 August poll showed that incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema won with a 60% share of the vote compared to Mundubile's 38%.

The day after the vote, security forces raided a property in the capital, Lusaka, linked to Mundubile, killing a former cabinet minister and arresting a number of other politicians.

The authorities accused the opposition of planning an armed insurgency, which they denied.

Following the raid, Mundubile went to a "secure location under the protection of an international human rights body due to threats made against him", his NRPUP party said.

ZNBC reports that the opposition leader, along with his running mate Makebi Zulu, had been protected by the United Nations in Lusaka.

It adds that the two are now being interviewed by "law enforcement officers" in the presence of their lawyers after a summons regarding "alleged activities that police say have the potential to threaten national security".

The opposition was unable to mount a legal challenge to the election outcome as the courts were sealed off by the authorities on Monday, the final day that a case could be filed.

Hichilema is due to be sworn in for a second term on 1 September.

articles.title: Andy Burnham says a united Ireland poll is 'off the table' during first NI visit
articles.summary: Andy Burnham said "we need to fix the things right in front of us in the here and now".
articles.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has ruled out calling a referendum on Irish unification, describing a border poll as "off the table".

The Labour leader said votes on Brexit and Scottish independence showed the "risks that come from those situations take a long time to heal".

Speaking during his first official visit to Northern Ireland, he said the focus should instead be on public services and tackling cost-of-living pressures.

"We need to fix the things right in front of us in the here and now," he told BBC News NI.

Burnham met Stormont's first and deputy first ministers, and the leaders of the Northern Ireland Assembly's main parties.

His visit comes amid calls from the power-sharing executive for increased funding from the government to ease budget pressures.

The four-party coalition has yet to set a budget nearly five months into the financial year.

Stormont departments are facing a shortfall of up to £1.6bn , according to a spending watchdog.

Burnham said he wanted to have "an honest exchange" with political leaders in Northern Ireland.

"There are things that we would say if we can work together, have a look at where possible savings can be made or where things can be done differently, it's right and proper that I ask for those assurances," he added.

Burnham was also asked about the prospect of calling a referendum on whether Northern Ireland should remain part of the UK or join with the Republic of Ireland.

The prime minister replied: "Well obviously I'm here as I said earlier to listen and I will take a collaborative approach, but some issues will be off the table and that is one issue that will be off the table.

"Because we've got to focus on bringing people together as best we can."

Burnham cited the 2016 EU referendum and the 2014 vote on Scottish independence.

"What we find is that the risks that come from those situations take a long time to heal and it sets you right back, and you can't focus on what's right in front of us here and now," he added.

"The cost-of-living pressures that are hurting people in Northern Ireland, the need to get that budget set so that public services can function as they should."

He continued: "A decade since the Brexit referendum I think we've had too much division, too much arguing, too much backward-looking.

"We need to fix the things right in the here and now."

Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader Gavin Robinson welcomed the opportunity to engage with the prime minister.

He said Burnham's remarks on a border poll were "particularly encouraging" and were "putting to bed the nonsense" discussed in recent months.

Robinson said "clearly there are issues" around the budgetary settlement for Northern Ireland and it would form a key part of the DUP's talks with the prime minister.

Sinn Féin leader Mary Lou McDonald said the Irish republican party's delegation had a "very frank and very forthright" meeting with Burnham following his remarks in which he ruled out a referendum.

"We have put it to him very strongly that burying his head in the sand is not a plan, not a strategy, not wise and not acceptable to us," she said.

Burnham said that people in Northern Ireland "want more breathing space from the cost of living, good, well-paid jobs and opportunities for their children".

"Political point scoring in the past has made this harder, not easier," he said in a statement ahead of his trip.

"We need to be better, so I want to work with the Northern Ireland Executive and the main political parties to try and make a real difference to communities here, and that's the message I'll be taking into my meetings later."

Before meeting politicians, the prime minister heard from young people about the issues that impact their lives and their aspirations for the future.

He spoke to teenagers and staff involved in mentoring schemes within Belfast's creative music scene - which seeks to elevate artists and promote the city as a UNESCO City of Music.

Earlier on Thursday, Burnham travelled to south Wales - his first official visit to the country since he became prime minister.

Before the trip Burnham announced plans to bring together the leaders of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland in the autumn for a summit to help boost the UK economy.

Speaking ahead of Burnham's visit, First Minister Michelle O'Neill called for a "fair budget settlement that actually works for public services".

"The reality is that we are so underfunded - have been for years," she told reporters on Wednesday.

"If Andy Burnham wants to make a difference, then he can make a difference by actually changing the funding arrangement, because what we have currently does not cut it."

Talks between Treasury officials and the executive have been taking place over the summer.

He said the executive could consider more "self-help" in the form of revenue-raising, but where there are "significant" budgetary pressures he wanted to be able to help.

articles.body: Raksha Bandhan is one of the most auspicious festivals that celebrates the unique relationship between brothers and sisters. It falls on a full moon day, or Purnima Tithi, that occurs in the month of Shravana. In 2026, Raksha Bandhan will be celebrated on a Friday, August 28. On this day, sisters all across India will tie the sacred Rakhi thread on their brothers’ wrists and pray for their welfare.While Raksha Bandhan is indeed all about the exchange of gifts, the timing of the ritual is also considered to be of great significance. According to the Hindu Panchang, tying the Rakhi should be done during an auspicious time and must be avoided during Bhadra Kaal. In order to determine an auspicious time to tie the Rakhi, it is important to consult the Panchang.Raksha Bandhan 2026 date and Purnima TithiRaksha Bandhan 2026 will be celebrated on August 28. According to Drik Panchang calculations, Shravana Purnima Tithi will begin at around 9:08 AM on August 27 and will end at 9:48 AM on the following day, August 28. Hence since the auspicious time to perform the Rakhi ceremony lies on August 28 (after Bhadra), Raksha Bandhan will be celebrated on a Friday.It must be noted that the sunrise and ceremony timing may vary from city to city. For instance, according to Panchang, the Rakhi ceremony is said to be performed between 6:23 AM to 9:48 AM in Maharashtra on Raksha Bandhan 2026. Hence, in order to ensure accuracy, it is best to check the Raksha Bandhan 2026 date and time according to your city.Bhadra Kaal on Raksha Bandhan 2026Bhadra Kaal is an inauspicious time for performing religious rituals. In the case of Raksha Bandhan, Panchang experts suggest that the Rakhi ceremony must be avoided completely during Bhadra. Bhadra Kaal will end before sunrise on August 28, which means that the Rakhi ceremony is not recommended on this day. However, there is an auspicious window of time after sunrise on August 28 for tying the Rakhi.This is also the reason why Raksha Bandhan 2026 will be celebrated on August 28 even though the Purnima Tithi commenced on August 27. The Rakhi ceremony must be performed only after Bhadra Kaal has ended, as per the Panchang.Raksha Bandhan 2026 shubh muhuratIt must be noted that the Raksha Bandhan ceremony timings vary from city to city. For instance, in Maharashtra, Raksha Bandhan 2026 is said to be performed after sunrise between 6:23 AM to 9:48 AM.It is recommended to choose an auspicious shubh muhurat after sunrise and before Bhadra Kaal (as per Panchang) for performing the Rakhi ceremony. In addition to this, people who follow a certain regional Panchang or family tradition may also refer to it before performing the ritual.Raksha Bandhan puja vidhiThe Raksha Bandhan ritual can be performed in a hassle-free manner. Here’s a simple Raksha Bandhan puja vidhi:First of all, prepare a puja area and make sure to keep the necessary items in a puja thali. A traditional Rakhi thali consists of Rakhi, roli (kumkum), rice grains, sandal paste, diya, sweets and flowers. In addition to these items, some people also keep a kalash in addition to other puja supplies.Both the brother and sister should offer prayers to their favorite deity and seek their blessings.The sister can apply tilak on her brother’s forehead and put a few grains of rice on the tilak.Now, the sister can tie the Rakhi around her brother’s wrist while chanting a prayer for his health, welfare and happiness.The brother then accepts the Rakhi and gives his sister a gift in return. In addition to this, the sister and her brother also exchange sweets and take blessings from elders. It is important to note that the Raksha Bandhan ceremony must be performed in a stress-free and positive manner.Rules to follow while tying RakhiThere are several rules to be kept in mind while tying Rakhi. Some of the most important rules include:Since Bhadra Kaal is considered to be an inauspicious time, the Rakhi ceremony must be avoided. As per Panchang, the Rakhi should be tied only after Bhadra has ended.The sister should make sure that the Rakhi is kept in the thali along with other puja items before the shubh muhurat. The sister must sit in front of the brother while performing the tilak and Rakhi ceremony according to one’s family tradition.It is essential to start the Rakhi ceremony with a smile and positive mindset. It is also advised to make sure that the Rakhi is tied comfortably rather than making it too tight.Although different regions and families may follow different customs, it is important not to overdo the festival. articles.title: From today, households across Great Britain can plug solar panels into a standard socket; 800W kits could supply up to 20% of home electricity use and save £110 a year
articles.summary: UK News: Households across Great Britain can now generate their own solar power using a standard three-pin wall socket, under new rules designed to cut energy .
articles.body: Households across Great Britain can now generate their own solar power using a standard three-pin wall socket, under new rules designed to cut energy bills and make clean electricity more accessible. The legal change, which came into force on 27 August 2026, allows people in England, Scotland and Wales to buy portable solar panel kits rated up to 800 watts and plug them directly into their home electricity supply without hiring an electrician. According to estimates from the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, the devices can provide up to 20 per cent of an average home's electricity use and save households up to £110 a year.The change comes as energy prices in Britain face fresh pressure. Energy regulator Ofgem has announced a 4 per cent rise in the domestic energy price cap from October, mainly because of higher wholesale fuel costs linked to continuing geopolitical tensions around Iran. Under the new rules, changes to the Plugs and Sockets etc. (Safety) Regulations 1994 and the Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002 through Statutory Instrument 2026/848 mean households no longer need specialist wiring or professional installation for small solar systems. Major retailers including Amazon, Currys, Argos and Wickes have announced plans to sell approved kits online and in their stores. "From this summer, we are giving more families the ability to power their homes with clean homegrown energy," said Miatta Fahnbulleh, the UK Energy Secretary, describing the technology as a simple and affordable way for households to manage their energy bills.Making solar easier for renters and flatsUntil now, home solar in Great Britain was mostly an option for property owners who could afford to spend thousands of pounds on permanent rooftop systems. The new plug-in technology is aimed particularly at renters, flat owners and people living in smaller terraced homes who may not be able to install traditional solar panels. The systems can use up to two solar panels connected to an 800-watt micro-inverter. The inverter changes the direct current produced by the panels into alternating current that can be used through a normal household electricity circuit. The electricity is used inside the home and first offsets power being consumed by appliances that are always running, such as fridges, Wi-Fi routers, televisions and devices on standby. Green energy groups welcomed the change, calling it an important step towards wider access to small-scale renewable power."This will bring cheap, clean power to households that have not been able to access the benefits of solar and batteries," said Chris Hewett, Chief Executive Officer of trade association Solar Energy UK. Trevor Hutchings, Chief Executive Officer of the Renewable Energy Association, described the move as a major step towards making renewable energy available to more people. "Our electricity prices are some of the highest because of our exposure to volatile international gas markets. Innovations like plug-in solar and the wider renewables roll out will help us bring down bills and strengthen our energy sovereignty," Hutchings said.Strict safety rules for plug-in systemsThe approval of plug-in solar systems follows safety testing of micro-inverters and household wiring. Government officials said British technical requirements are stricter than those used in some parts of continental Europe, where more than 500,000 balcony solar systems were connected in Germany during 2025. All approved British kits must have automatic anti-islanding protection. The system cuts power from the plug within 100 milliseconds if the device is unplugged or the local electricity supply fails. This prevents the exposed plug from remaining live and creating a risk of electric shock. The rules also place limits on how the systems can be used. Each household can have only one plug-in solar device. It must be connected directly to a fixed wall socket and cannot be used with an extension lead, multi-way adaptor or cable reel. Battery storage systems are not included in the new rules and cannot currently be connected through the plug-in route. Fire safety rules also restrict where the panels can be installed. They cannot be mounted on timber balconies, high-pressure laminate cladding or external walls that are undergoing safety work. Mounting systems must be non-permanent and reversible, while tenants and other residents need written permission from their landlord or freeholder before fixing panels to external structures.Growing demand for home solarThe new rules come as residential solar installations continue to grow across Great Britain. Data from the Microgeneration Certification Scheme recorded almost 150,000 certified rooftop solar installations in the first six months of 2026. That was 17 per cent higher than the previous record for the same period in 2025. Government estimates show that traditional rooftop solar can save homeowners up to £480 a year. However, officials expect plug-in systems to attract many more households because they are cheaper and easier to install. Similar systems typically cost between £400 and £600 in European markets. After installing a system, owners must enter its details on the official UK Plug-In Solar Registration portal. This will help local electricity network operators track the amount of small-scale generation connected to the grid. The new rules currently apply across England, Scotland and Wales. Northern Ireland is expected to consider similar measures under its own energy policies.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Kai Cenat’s morning took a bizarre turn when a woman arrived at his gate with a 2-year-old child and claimed that he was the girl’s father. The woman, who said her name was Yasmin, reportedly told Cenat that she had driven for 15 hours to meet him. Cenat strongly denied knowing her or being the child’s father.Kai Cenat denies woman’s paternity claim during tense encounterCenat said the woman arrived at around 10 a.m. with the young girl. He said she told him that the child was two years old and claimed that Cenat was her father.However, Cenat quickly rejected the claim. In the footage he showed on stream, he can be heard telling the woman, “That is not my daughter. No, it’s not. Who’s the mother? I’ve never seen you in my life.”Cenat also said that the child’s age made the claim hard for him to believe. He explained that he had been in a relationship for the last two years. According to Cenat, the child answered, “You.”That moment made the situation even stranger for him. Cenat said he felt that the child may have been coached before the meeting.“Y’all want to know the crazy thing? I didn’t even catch it on camera,” Cenat said while telling his viewers about the moment.He then joked about the situation, saying, “I said, ‘Oh, she trained the baby.’ Like, this baby a paid actor.”Kai Cenat refuses to let woman inside during bizarre encounterDespite the unusual claim, Cenat and his security team did not open the gate. His friend Davis later arrived during the confrontation. Cenat said Davis understood what was happening and jumped over a fence to make sure nobody could get inside.The situation eventually ended without a major fight. Cenat said he decided to give the woman and the child snacks and water. He also said he ordered an Uber for them to return to their hotel.Cenat explained that he did this partly because he felt sorry for the young girl.“The daughter looks so innocent,” he said.Cenat has continued to deny that the child is his daughter. The footage and his account of the encounter have now given his viewers more details about the unusual situation. However, the woman’s identity and her claim have not been independently confirmed.For now, Cenat’s side of the story is clear, he says he does not know the woman and strongly denies being the father of her 2-year-old daughter. The strange encounter has left viewers with many questions about what led to the unexpected visit.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Nepal floods: Aberdeen man's brother, uncle and cousin die
articles.summary: Barun Lamichhane, from Aberdeen, tells BBC Scotland News his uncle, brother and cousin all died but his parents and grandmother survived.
articles.body:
A Nepalese man living in Aberdeen has told BBC Scotland News he lost three close family members in the deadly flash floods that hit his home country on Wednesday.

Barun Lamichhane, 26, said his brother, uncle and cousin all died in the disaster - but that his mother, father and grandmother managed to escape.

Lamichhane said they managed to get away by "crawling like a baby" into the hillside.

More than 350 people have died, with more than 1,000 reported to be missing.

More than 350 killed in Nepal as experts warn of possible second flood

The deadly flood happened near the Nepal-Tibet border early on Wednesday.

Preliminary information suggested it had been caused by an earthquake.

However the US Geological Survey later said additional analysis indicated that the "seismic energy was instead generated by a landslide".

Lamichhane is from the village of Betrawati, which was one of the many areas badly affected.

He graduated from the University of the West of Scotland in International Events Management a few weeks ago.

He said: "I was sleeping and my sister woke me up and said 'in our village there is nothing - like everything is gone'.

"At that time, I'm just a blank, I can't even think.

"They are saying that our home, everything, is gone. Nothing is left."

Lamichhane said he fears he has also lost many more friends and neighbours in the disaster as well as his brother, uncle and cousin.

He said his mother, Tulasha Lamichhane, father, Netra Prasad Lamichhane, and grandmother, Krishna Kumari Lamichhane, escaped.

They were all in different locations when the flood hit.

He said they were now sheltering in a school that is being used as a refuge for those who survived.

Lamichhane said he "can't express" the pain he is feeling.

More stories from North East Scotland, Orkney and Shetland

Listen to news from North East Scotland on BBC Sounds

Thirty-three people from the UK, including a 13-year-old girl and 14-year-old boy, are among the hundreds who are missing following the deadly floods.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK had offered £5m to help the Nepalese government , saying it was a "very distressing and devastating situation".

The UK Foreign Office said it was working closely with Nepalese authorities "following concerning reports of British nationals who are missing".

It has encouraged Brits to follow local guidance and "remain alert to the changing situation".

Dramatic CCTV footage showed a wall of water and mud hitting buildings near a border crossing.

And video filmed from inside a bus in Trishuli captured dozens of people trying to flee a flood surge that was surging through the valley.

articles.title: Blake Lively awarded $400,000 of $8m she claimed for legal fees in Justin Baldoni battle
articles.summary: A judge awards less than Lively requested to cover her legal fees to fight a defamation case he filed.
articles.body:
Actress Blake Lively has been awarded $400,000 (£340,000) of the $8m (£6.9m) she tried to claim from her former co-star Justin Baldoni to cover her legal fees and costs to fight a defamation case he brought.

Lively initially sued Baldoni, her co-star and director of the 2024 film It Ends With Us for sexual harassment and retaliation, before he countersued for defamation.

A judge dismissed his defamation complaint in 2025, and she argued she was entitled to $7.5m (£6.4m) to cover her lawyers' fees and $540,000 (£460,000) for other costs.

But the judge said she should receive considerably less - a total of $407,451 - because she requested money for more people and time than were necessary to defend the defamation claim.

She should not have claimed money for other "intertwined" costs to do with the wider legal battle, and took a "blunderbuss approach" to calculating how many hours of lawyers' time she could claim for, the judge said.

Baldoni denied harassing Lively or orchestrating a smear campaign against her.

Earlier this year, the judge dismissed parts of Lively's lawsuit against him including the sexual harassment element. The following month, the pair agreed a settlement to end the case.

The judge allowed Lively to recover some expenses under a 2023 California law designed to protect sexual harassment accusers from retaliatory defamation lawsuits brought by the men they accused.

Both sides painted US District Judge Lewis Liman's latest decision as a victory.

Lively's lawyers said: "This first-ever award of fees and costs under this California law is historic, and demonstrates that there are real consequences of bringing retaliatory lawsuits.

"As we have said from day one, Blake Lively's case was never about money – it was about accountability."

Baldoni's lawyer Bryan Freedman said: "The ruling is a significant victory for my clients and sends a clear message that, no matter how powerful you may be, the courtroom is not a place to take advantage of the law for your own personal gain."

articles.title: King Charles 'heartbroken' by deadly Nepal flash floods
articles.summary: Some 33 people from the UK are missing, including a 13-year-old girl and 14-year-old boy.
articles.body:
The King says he and Queen Camilla are "heartbroken" by the deadly flash floods near the Nepal-Tibet border, as 33 people from the UK are missing including a 13-year-old girl and 14-year-old boy.

The Prince and Princess of Wales also expressed their shock, saying they were "thinking of everyone caught up in this terrible disaster".

The death toll from the floods has risen to at least 359, with more than 1,300 people missing, 644 of whom are tourists according to Nepali authorities.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK has offered £5m to help the Nepalese government following the floods, adding it was a "very distressing and devastating situation".

King Charles said that he and the Queen were sending their "most profound sympathy to all those who have so tragically lost their loved ones".

"Many in the United Kingdom have strong, deep and personal ties to this part of the world," the King's statement continued.

"We feel deeply for the many families awaiting anxiously the news of friends and relations.

"Our hearts go out also to the families of all the police and armed forces personnel who lost their lives while carrying out their courageous duty in the service of others."

The prime minister and the Foreign Office in the UK have urged people to follow local guidance and remain alert to the changing situation, as officials in Nepal warn of a possible secondary flood risk near the Bhote Koshi river.

The Foreign Office added it was working closely with Nepalese authorities.

British resident Pramod Pudel, who lives in East Sussex but is originally from Nepal, told BBC Radio Sussex on Thursday that "nothing remains" where his family lives and he is flying back to search for his wife, mother, brother and uncle.

"It's a very, very difficult time for me and for my family and my country at this moment, but obviously I have to go and see what's happening there," he said.

"A lot of people are missing and there is no information regarding who is missing, where they are. Nobody can contact each other and all the bridges are broken, so you can't cross the land.

"There's no power, no electricity, so I can't contact anyone, so it's a very difficult time not knowing what's happening."

Tour companies including Alpine Eco Trek, The Trekkers' Society, Himalayan Glacier US, Kailash Journeys and Fishtail Tours have reported missing British nationals while on trips with the companies.

Alpine Eco Trek said it has not been able to establish contact with 12 Britons who were booked on a tour to Mount Kailash and were in the region when the flash floods struck.

The company's travel logs which were shared with the Press Association, with a 13-year-old girl the youngest person missing.

Four of the firm's Nepali tour guides are also missing.

Mount Kailash - a peak in the Himalayas near the border between Nepal and Tibet - is considered the spiritual home of the Hindu god Shiva.

The journey to the mountain is part of the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, a sacred pilgrimage for Hindus.

The pilgrimage had only recently resumed after being disrupted first by the pandemic and then by tensions between India and China.

The Trekkers' Society said nine UK nationals on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash are missing after they crossed the Nepal-Tibet border. Four males aged between 14 and 50, and five females aged 40 to 53 remain missing.

Himalayan Glacier US had 47 guests on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, with two in the group being British citizens.

Kailash Journeys reported 27 guests and staff were missing, with two British men in the group.

Fishtail Tours said one British person on its tour was missing.

The flood hit early on Wednesday in Rasuwa, just north of Nepal's capital Kathmandu.

Preliminary information suggested it was caused by an earthquake, but the US Geological Survey said additional analysis indicated "the seismic energy was instead generated by a landslide."

It said a magnitude 5.2 seismic event caused by a "glacial collapse and debris flow" occurred near the border at 08:37 local time on Wednesday.

articles.title: US ICE officer accused of shooting man in Minneapolis released from Texas jail
articles.summary: US News: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer accused of shooting a man during the immigration crackdown in Minneapolis and allegedly lying abo.
articles.body: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer accused of shooting a man during the immigration crackdown in Minneapolis and allegedly lying about the incident was released from a Texas jail on Thursday after a federal judge declined to order his return to Minnesota.Christian Castro walked out of a detention centre in Brownsville at dawn and left in an SUV after briefly acknowledging reporters and camera operators waiting outside.US District Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr, in an order issued Wednesday, said he could not prevent a county sheriff from releasing Castro or compel Texas Governor Greg Abbott to approve his extradition to Minnesota.Castro faces assault and false-reporting charges in Minnesota over the January 14 shooting of 24-year-old Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis.ICE officer accused of shooting man through doorCastro is accused of firing a gun through the front door of a Minneapolis home and hitting Sosa-Celis in the leg. Prosecutors allege he later falsely claimed that Sosa-Celis and another man had attacked an ICE officer with a broom handle and a snow shovel.A Minnesota judge issued a nationwide arrest warrant for Castro in May. He was arrested by authorities, including the state's Bureau of Criminal Apprehension, in Cameron County on May 29.Minnesota officials had sought his extradition, but Castro remained in custody in Brownsville, near the US-Mexico border. Under Texas law, he had to be released after 90 days unless extradited.Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison had sought a temporary restraining order to block Castro's release or secure his return to Minnesota.Texas Governor Abbott yet to decide on extraditionTexas lawyers argued that the federal court could not intervene while Abbott's decision on the extradition request was still pending.Abbott is awaiting an internal state investigation into whether Castro qualifies as a "fugitive" under the US Constitution's Extradition Clause.Judge Rodriguez said the case was not yet ripe for adjudication, noting that Minnesota could not base its claims on the possibility that Abbott might violate his legal obligations in the future.The judge also said extradition laws do not specify how long a governor can take to decide on such a request.Abbott had earlier said he would not immediately respond to Minnesota's extradition request, citing an ongoing investigation into alleged fraud involving government social service programmes in the state.Minnesota fears Castro could flee to MexicoMinnesota officials have warned that Castro could flee the US following his release. They cited calls he allegedly made from jail to a woman in Mexico, during which he discussed marrying her and buying a house there after his release.The judge acknowledged that Castro could potentially flee the country but said the threat alone was not enough for the court to intervene.Following the ruling, Ellison said his office would continue pursuing the case. Abbott's office welcomed the decision, saying the governor has a duty to carefully examine the merits of extradition requests.The ruling has intensified a political clash between Texas and Minnesota officials over immigration enforcement and the handling of criminal cases involving ICE personnel.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Meet Scott Merrow, the 14-year-old New Hampshire gamer who built a 3D-printed adaptive VR controller after he found he could not grip the standard left-hand controller
articles.summary: US News: For 14-year-old Scott Merrow of Auburn, New Hampshire, playing video games has always meant finding his own way to use a standard controller. A gamer .
articles.body: For 14-year-old Scott Merrow of Auburn, New Hampshire, playing video games has always meant finding his own way to use a standard controller. A gamer who enjoys playing virtual reality games with his friends, Scott has a condition called symbrachydactyly, in which fingers may be underdeveloped or may not develop at all, according to Boston Children's Hospital.According to Wmur, Scott refers to his left hand as his 'little hand'. While playing with a traditional game controller, he developed his own way of using it. He would keep the controller in his lap and divide its controls between his left and right hands."And I'd basically just section the controller off, so half would be my little hand; the other half would be my right hand that really just adapted to it," Scott says. "I can't explain how it works, because I grew up with it. I don't know what it's like to have two hands," he adds.That approach worked for a traditional controller, but virtual reality gaming created a different problem. VR systems use a headset and controllers designed to be held in each hand. Scott could not grip the left-hand controller in the usual way, so instead of giving up on the games, he decided to build something that could work for him."This was how it all started out," Scott, an eighth grader at Auburn Village School, says while referring to the first of three versions of his adaptive VR controller.From a school project to a working prototypeScott began the project as a school assignment and asked his uncle, Brandyn Lewis, a mechanical engineer, to help him. Lewis agreed, and the two began working together on the design and programming.The project went through several versions as they tried to solve different problems. Scott worked with Lewis at his shop at New Hampshire Ball Bearings, where they continued developing the controller.Lewis said he enjoyed helping Scott work through the problems involved in creating the device. He also praised the teenager for continuing to work on the project despite the challenges involved."I like being able to try to help him solve problems, you know, come up with solutions that will benefit him. He's put a lot of work into this, a lot of effort, to step through this and stuck with it, which has impressed me," Lewis says.Scott's third prototype uses a 3D-printed sleeve that wraps around his arm. A sensor inside the sleeve can be pressed by Scott. The system then uses a computer to interpret different amounts of pressure and send signals to the controller.In simple terms, the pressure Scott applies to the sensor is used as an input. The computer reads that input and tells the VR controller which buttons to press. This allows him to operate controls without having to grip the standard left-hand controller in the usual way.Moment controller finally workedThe third prototype gave Scott a moment he had not experienced before. While testing the adaptive controller, he was able to use it to throw a paper airplane in a game using the left-handed controls. "Oh!" Scott said during the test. "I threw it, by the way."The controller is not yet a final product. Scott says there are still adjustments that need to be made as he continues working on it.His been presenting the invention through the Invention Convention, a worldwide education programme for students from kindergarten through Grade 12.After winning second place in the New England region, he is set to travel to Michigan for the national convention next month.Sharing the experienceScott's mother, Kristine Merrow, said he has been comfortable explaining his invention and showing people how it works. She said he has been able to speak about the project without needing much practice."Seeing him kind of hold court as other people go around and with his board and talk about this and stand up, and some of the videos he's made, that's with zero practice," she said. "Scott can kind of naturally talk to people."Scott has also been sharing his experience on social media and advocating for the adaptive community. A post about his project in the WMUR U Local Facebook group had received nearly 7,000 likes.His parents have supported his work throughout the process. His father, Barry Merrow, said the family is proud of Scott and excited that he wants to continue with the project."(We are) beyond proud of him," Barry says. "I mean, he really is excited for this, and I'm excited that he wants to do this."As Scott continues making adjustments to his adaptive VR controller, he is also encouraging other children who may face similar difficulties not to stop trying."Don't give up," he says. "Just keep trying. Just figure out another way. There's always going to be another path."Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
